audit.whatIsWrong: The content and full charts read Graves/Graves/Graves/Skill/Skill/Graves/Skill; the packet chart reads Skill/Skill/Graves/Zaahen/Skill/Graves/Zaahen. The whys[] text matches the packet word for word — whys[0] 'Level 1 is even', whys[1] 'Level 2 stays even', whys[3] "Levels 4-5 are Zaahen's", whys[6] '2+ items is Zaahen'. Four rows were simply transcribed wrong.
audit.why: This one is unambiguous: the prose literally names the side for each row and four of them disagree with the token beside them. 47.35% over 3487 games is the largest sample in the slice.
audit.corrected: win[0], win[1], win[3], win[6] and the matching phases sides aligned to the packet; ratings 5/5/6/4/5/6/3.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown appears anywhere on the page — the packet counts 1 sequencing cue — despite the entire win condition being 'schedule your pattern around its cooldown'.
audit.why: His R is 110/95/80s, his W pull is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s and his E dash is 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s. 110 seconds is a whole wave cycle of freedom; without the number 'punish the gap' means nothing.
audit.corrected: 110s added to breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[2].d; the W pull's 850 range now anchors the 4-5 advice.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. First, the missing one: Zaahen's passive says that when filled with Determination he gains increased Attack Damage AND CAN REVIVE, and Determination stacks off his attacks and abilities against champions. Nothing on the page mentions a revive. That single fact rewrites 'never let a trade become a brawl' from a preference into a hard rule — a long fight is what fills his bar. His W also pulls you toward him at 850 range and his Q recast knocks up, neither of which is stated. Second, the Graves-side boilerplate: 'the Smoke Screen blind' / 'the blind' / 'blind fights' four times (W reduces sight range and slows on impact, it is not a blind) and dosFull[2] 'Hold R as the disengage knockback' (Collateral Damage has no displacement in its text).
audit.why: A Graves who burns his ultimate to finish a Zaahen at full Determination gets a revived Zaahen with bonus AD and no 100-second answer left.
audit.corrected: Revive and Determination added to whys[6], phases[6] and late; the pull and knock-up added to whys[3], phases[3] and spikes[1]; blind and knockback removed.

audit.why: Common mistakes are behavioural and not split by elo.

edits.before: Four shells of buckshot win any level-1 face-off — trade autos point-blank where every pellet lands.
edits.after: Neither kit has a spell that decides anything yet — farm the wave and take no face-off at all.

edits.before: E online — dash-reload weaving starts: auto, E for the grit armor and reset, auto again. Most champs lose this flat.
edits.after: E online and the dash-reload weave starts, but neither kit is fully online yet, so level 2 stays a stand-off.

edits.before: Trade in shell rhythm: two autos and out. Track Ultimate; your armor stacks from E make his short trades unprofitable.
edits.after: Trade in shell rhythm: two autos and out — his 850-range pull drags you straight back if Quickdraw is already spent.

edits.before: Collateral Damage adds an execute and a disengage knockback in one — hold it for either, never for chip.
edits.after: Collateral Damage is a 100-second nuke that chunks him out of his commit — never spend it on chip.

edits.before: You out-skirmish but the crit scalers pass you — convert to picks with smoke-screen blinds and R snipes.
edits.after: A full Determination bar means bonus AD and a revive — keep every fight short, never let it extend.

edits.before: - Zaahen Ultimate: matchup-defining — His big cooldown — punish the gap while it is down. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E dash for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Zaahen Ultimate: matchup-defining — 110 seconds at rank 1 — punish the whole gap while it is down. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E dash for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.

edits.before: Hold R as the disengage knockback
edits.after: Hold R to finish, never to chip

edits.before: Zaahen spends Ultimate early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Zaahen spends his 110-second ultimate early — the closest thing here to a guarantee.

edits.before: Play assassin-marksman: smoke their engage, E through fights for armor, and save R as either the execute or the peel knockback. Crit carries out-DPS you — picks don't care.
edits.after: Play assassin-marksman: smoke their engage, E through fights for armor, and save the 100-second R to finish, never to chip. Crit carries out-DPS you — picks don't care.

edits.before: Your W smoke blinds tower dives and breaks gank pathing — drop it on arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip you win.
edits.after: Your W smoke nearsights tower dives and breaks gank pathing — drop it on arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip you win.

edits.before: Level 3 is Graves — Buckshot plus the Smoke Screen blind and reload autos simply out-DPS him up close.
edits.after: Level 3 is Graves — Buckshot plus a Smoke Screen that blanks his sight out-damages him up close.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are Zaahen's: his early ult engage punishes a spent Quickdraw — do not burn E for damage in this window.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are Zaahen's: his 850-range pull drags you back onto a spent Quickdraw — never burn E for damage here.

edits.before: 2+ items is Zaahen — he out-brawls a squishy, peel-less Graves in any extended fight, so keep everything short and ranged.
edits.after: 2+ items is Zaahen — a full Determination bar gives him bonus AD and a revive, so never let a fight run long enough to fill it.

edits.before: His early ult hunts a spent Quickdraw — hold E as an exit, not a poke tool.
edits.after: His pull and knock-up hunt a spent Quickdraw — hold E as an exit, not a poke tool.

edits.before: Open patient — levels 1-2 are pure farming — then hit the gas at 3, where Buckshot, the blind, and reload autos out-DPS him point-blank. The catch: his ult comes online around 4-5 and it hunts a spent Quickdraw, so from that point E is an exit, not a damage tool. Trade hard inside your window, then give the 4-5 stretch real respect.
edits.after: Open patient — levels 1-2 are pure farming — then hit the gas at 3, where Buckshot, the smoke's sight denial and reload autos out-DPS him point-blank. The catch: his 850-range pull drags you back onto a spent Quickdraw from 4-5 onward, so from that point E is an exit, not a damage tool. Trade hard inside your window, then respect the 4-5 stretch.

edits.before: Level 6 balances the ledger — your burst chunks him out of ult commits — and first item tips it back to you: the lethality spike kills through his sustain before it ticks. Look for one-rotation kills off grass angles and blind fights he cannot answer. Just never let a trade become a brawl; the longer it runs, the more his healing does.
edits.after: Level 6 balances the ledger — your burst chunks him out of ult commits — and first item tips it back to you: the lethality spike kills through his sustain before it ticks. Look for one-rotation kills off grass angles and smoke he cannot see through. Never let a trade become a brawl: his Q and his R both heal him, and every hit he lands fills Determination.

edits.before: Two-plus items his extended-fight brawling beats a peel-less Graves, so your rules harden: burst, blind, Quickdraw out, reset. Play sides with escape routes mapped, group when he shows, and use your range to chunk him before fights start. If he reaches you at full HP with cooldowns up, that fight was lost before it began — do not take it.
edits.after: Two-plus items his extended-fight brawling beats a peel-less Graves, so your rules harden: burst, smoke, Quickdraw out, reset. Every hit he lands fills Determination, and a full bar is bonus AD plus a revive — a long fight literally rebuilds him. If he reaches you at full HP with cooldowns up, that fight was lost before it began — do not take it.

notes: Zaahen's kit is present but UNNAMED — every ability text is there, packet.enemyAbilities is null, so the page's habit of writing 'his ult' and 'Ultimate' is the only option available and I left it. The revive on his passive was absent from the entire page and is the most important fact in the matchup; it is now in three fields. I did NOT touch the claim that his ultimate is online 'around 4-5' — see questionsForUser; I replaced the 4-5 rationale with his W pull, which is verified, rather than assert an unlock level I cannot confirm for a non-standard champion.
